questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a flower?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a component of a flower?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Spines.

Key Points

  • Spines are not a component of a flower; they are modified leaves, stems, or stipules that are typically hard, pointed, and meant for protection.
  • Flowers are reproductive structures in angiosperms (flowering plants) and typically consist of four main parts: androecium, corolla, calyx, and gynoecium.
  • The primary role of spines is to protect the plant from herbivores and reduce water loss, especially in arid environments.
  • Unlike the other options listed (androecium, corolla, and calyx), spines do not play a role in the reproductive process of the flower.

Additional Information

  • Androecium
    • The androecium is the collective term for the stamens in a flower. Each stamen typically consists of a filament and an anther, where pollen is produced.
    • It is the male reproductive part of the flower.
  • Corolla
    • The corolla is the collective term for the petals of a flower.
    • Petals are often brightly colored to attract pollinators.
  • Calyx
    • The calyx is the collective term for the sepals of a flower.
    • Sepals are typically green and provide protection to the flower bud before it opens.
  • Gynoecium
    • The gynoecium is the collective term for the female reproductive parts of a flower, consisting of one or more carpels.
    • Each carpel typically includes an ovary, style, and stigma.

questions.question: Where was the Hindu College established in the year 1791?
questions.questionHtml: Where was the Hindu College established in the year 1791?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Benaras.

Key Points

  • The Hindu College was established in the year 1791.
  • It was founded in the city of Benaras, which is now known as Varanasi.
  • The institution was set up to provide Western education to Indians.
  • It played a significant role in the Indian Renaissance and the spread of modern education in India.

Additional Information

  • Hindu College:
    • The Hindu College in Benaras was one of the earliest institutions to provide a structured curriculum for Western-style education in India.
    • It was founded by influential citizens of Benaras, including Raja Rammohan Roy.
    • The college was established with the aim of imparting modern education in various fields such as science, mathematics, and the humanities.
    • It later evolved into the Central Hindu School and eventually became a part of Banaras Hindu University (BHU).
  • Banaras Hindu University (BHU):
    • Established in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, BHU is one of the largest residential universities in Asia.
    • BHU offers courses in various fields including arts, science, engineering, medicine, and agriculture.
    • The university is renowned for its research and academic excellence.
    • It has a sprawling campus spread over 1,300 acres in Varanasi.
  • Raja Rammohan Roy:
    • Raja Rammohan Roy was a prominent social and educational reformer in India during the early 19th century.
    • He is often called the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" due to his efforts in promoting modern education and social reforms.
    • He was an advocate for the abolition of practices such as Sati and child marriage.
    • His contributions laid the foundation for the development of modern Indian society.

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • The Gulf of Mannar is a large shallow bay forming part of the Laccadive Sea in the Indian Ocean.
  • It lies between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka, specifically between Tamil Nadu and the Northern Province of Sri Lanka.
  • The Gulf of Mannar is renowned for its rich biodiversity and is home to the Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park, which is one of the richest coastal regions in Asia.
  • This region is famous for its pearl banks and is often referred to as the Pearl of the Indian Ocean.

Additional Information

  • Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
    • It is a protected area in the Gulf of Mannar and covers an area of about 560 square kilometers.
    • The park is known for its coral reefs, seagrasses, and mangroves, which provide habitat for numerous marine species.
    • It is home to endangered species such as the dugong, sea turtles, and various species of dolphins and whales.
    • The park is part of the larger Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, which is recognized by UNESCO.
  • Geographical Significance
    • The Gulf of Mannar acts as a natural boundary between India and Sri Lanka.
    • This region is historically significant as it has been a major trading route for centuries.
    • The Mannar Island, located in the gulf, is known for its historical importance and natural beauty.
    • The shallow waters and coral reefs make it a popular destination for marine research and ecotourism.
  • Environmental Concerns
    • The region faces environmental challenges such as coral bleaching, overfishing, and pollution.
    • Conservation efforts are in place to protect the unique marine biodiversity of the Gulf of Mannar.
    • Local communities are involved in sustainable fishing practices to preserve the ecological balance.
    • There are ongoing initiatives to promote awareness and education about marine conservation in the area.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-tax revenue source for the government?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is an example of a non-tax revenue source for the government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fees and fines.

Key Points

  • Non-tax revenue refers to the recurring income earned by the government from sources other than taxes.
  • Fees and fines are common examples of non-tax revenue. Fees are payments made to the government for specific services or activities (e.g., passport fees, court fees), while fines are penalties imposed for violating laws or regulations.
  • Non-tax revenue sources help the government fund its operations without increasing the tax burden on citizens.
  • Other examples of non-tax revenue include interest receipts on loans given by the government, dividends from public sector enterprises, and income from government property.

Additional Information

  • Personal income tax:
    • It is a direct tax levied on the income of individuals.
    • The rate of personal income tax varies based on income slabs and is progressive in nature, meaning higher income earners pay a higher percentage in taxes.
  • Corporate income tax:
    • This is a tax imposed on the net income or profit of corporations.
    • It is a significant source of revenue for the government and is also a direct tax.
  • Value-added tax (VAT):
    • VAT is an indirect tax levied on the value added to goods and services at each stage of production or distribution.
    • Consumers ultimately bear the cost of VAT as it is included in the purchase price of goods and services.
  • Non-tax revenue sources:
    • These include all government revenue sources that do not fall under the category of taxes.
    • Examples include fees for services, fines and penalties, dividends from public enterprises, interest receipts, and revenue from government properties.

questions.question: Which of the following plants is used to cure cold and cough?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following plants is used to cure cold and cough?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tulsi.

Key Points

  • Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum), also known as Holy Basil, is a revered medicinal plant in India.
  • It is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to treat cold, cough, and other respiratory ailments.
  • Tulsi leaves are known to have antibacterial, antiviral, and antifungal properties, which help in relieving infections causing cold and cough.
  • Consumption of Tulsi tea or Tulsi-infused water can boost immunity and provide relief from respiratory disorders.

Additional Information

  • Babool (Acacia nilotica)
    • Babool tree has various medicinal uses, including in dental care, skin care, and as a remedy for diarrhea and dysentery.
    • Its bark and leaves are commonly used in traditional medicine.
  • Jamun (Syzygium cumini)
    • Jamun fruit and seeds are used in Ayurvedic medicine to manage diabetes.
    • It is also beneficial for digestive health and in treating ulcers.
  • Arjun (Terminalia arjuna)

    • Ashoka's transformation post-Kalinga War is well-documented in his rock and pillar edicts.
  • Buddhism

    • Ashoka's patronage played a significant role in the spread of Buddhism across India and beyond.
    • Ashoka convened the Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) to discuss the teachings and spread of Buddhism.
    • His efforts in promoting Buddhism included sending emissaries and missionaries to various parts of Asia, including Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, and Central Asia.

questions.question: Grignard reagent is represented as:
questions.questionHtml: Grignard reagent is represented as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is CH₃-Mg-Cl.

Key Points

  • Grignard reagents are organomagnesium compounds which are commonly represented as R-Mg-X, where R is an organic group and X is a halogen.
  • In the given options, CH₃-Mg-Cl (Methylmagnesium chloride) fits this representation.
  • Grignard reagents are highly reactive and are used in various organic synthesis reactions, particularly for forming carbon-carbon bonds.
  • They were discovered by the French chemist Victor Grignard, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1912 for this discovery.

Additional Information

  • Grignard Reagent:
    • Grignard reagents are typically prepared by reacting an alkyl or aryl halide with magnesium metal in an anhydrous ether solvent.
    • They are strong nucleophiles and strong bases, making them very useful in organic chemistry for forming new carbon-carbon bonds.
    • The general formula for a Grignard reagent is R-Mg-X, where R can be an alkyl, aryl, or vinyl group, and X is usually a halogen like chlorine, bromine, or iodine.
    • Due to their high reactivity, Grignard reagents must be handled under an inert atmosphere (such as nitrogen or argon) to prevent them from reacting with moisture or oxygen in the air.
  • Victor Grignard:
    • François Auguste Victor Grignard was a French chemist who discovered the Grignard reagent, which revolutionized the field of organic chemistry.
    • His discovery allowed for the formation of carbon-carbon bonds, which is fundamental in the synthesis of a wide variety of organic compounds.
    • He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1912 for this significant contribution.
  • Applications of Grignard Reagents:
    • Grignard reagents are used to form various types of carbon-carbon bonds, making them invaluable in the synthesis of alcohols, acids, and other organic compounds.
    • They can react with carbonyl compounds (such as aldehydes and ketones) to form secondary and tertiary alcohols.
    • They are also used in the synthesis of carboxylic acids by reacting with carbon dioxide.
    • In addition to their use in academic research, Grignard reagents are also used in the pharmaceutical and chemical industries for the synthesis of complex organic molecules.

questions.question: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1931.

Key Points

  • The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and the then Viceroy of India, Lord Irwin.
  • This pact marked the end of the civil disobedience movement led by the Indian National Congress against British rule in India.
  • Under the terms of the pact, the British Government agreed to release all political prisoners who had been detained during the civil disobedience movement.
  • Mahatma Gandhi, representing the Indian National Congress, agreed to discontinue the civil disobedience movement and participate in the Second Round Table Conference in London.

Additional Information

  • Gandhi-Irwin Pact
    • The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was a political agreement signed by Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy of India, Lord Irwin, in 1931.
    • It was a significant event in the Indian freedom struggle, which led to the cessation of the civil disobedience movement that was initiated against the British Salt Tax.
    • The pact included several concessions by the British Government, such as the withdrawal of all ordinances and prosecutions, release of prisoners arrested for participating in the salt march, and the return of confiscated properties of the satyagrahis.
    • Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference in London as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.
  • Civil Disobedience Movement
    • Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, the Civil Disobedience Movement aimed at disobeying certain laws, demands, and commands of the British government, particularly the Salt Act.
    • The movement began with the Dandi March, where Gandhi and his followers marched to the Arabian Sea coast to produce salt from seawater in defiance of British laws.
    • This movement attracted widespread participation from various sections of Indian society and was a crucial step towards India's independence.
    • The movement saw significant government repression, including the arrest of thousands of protesters and leaders.
  • Second Round Table Conference
    • The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in September 1931 and was attended by Mahatma Gandhi as the representative of the Indian National Congress.
    • The conference aimed to discuss constitutional reforms in India and the future governance of the country.
    • Despite the discussions, the conference did not result in any significant agreements, leading to Gandhi's return to India and the resumption of the civil disobedience movement.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of current?
questions.questionHtml: What is the SI unit of current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ampere.

Key Points

  • The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere, symbolized as A.
  • It is named after André-Marie Ampère, a French physicist and mathematician who is considered one of the founders of the science of classical electromagnetism.
  • One Ampere is defined as the flow of one coulomb of charge per second.
  • It is a fundamental unit in the International System of Units (SI), and it is used to quantify the amount of electric charge passing a point in an electric circuit per unit time.

Additional Information

  • Ohm (Ω)
    • The Ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.
    • Named after German physicist Georg Simon Ohm, it quantifies the resistance in a circuit.
    • One Ohm is defined as the resistance between two points of a conductor when a constant potential difference of 1 Volt, applied to these points, produces a current of 1 Ampere.
  • Volt (V)
    • The Volt is the SI unit of electric potential, electric potential difference, and electromotive force.
    • Named after the Italian physicist Alessandro Volta, it measures the potential difference between two points.
    • One Volt is defined as the potential difference that will drive one Ampere of current against one Ohm of resistance.
  • Metre (m)
    • The Metre is the SI unit of length.
    • It is defined as the distance traveled by light in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds.
    • It is a fundamental unit in the metric system and is used to measure distance.

questions.question: Name a common electrolyte disorder that occurs when the amount of sodium in your blood becomes abnormally low.
questions.questionHtml: Name a common electrolyte disorder that occurs when the amount of sodium in your blood becomes abnormally low.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hyponatremia.

Key Points

  • Hyponatremia is a condition where the sodium level in the blood is lower than normal.
  • Sodium is an essential electrolyte that helps regulate water balance in and around cells.
  • Common causes of hyponatremia include excessive fluid intake, certain medications, and conditions like heart failure or kidney disease.
  • Symptoms of hyponatremia can range from mild (nausea, headache) to severe (confusion, seizures, coma).

Additional Information

  • Hyperkalemia
    • Hyperkalemia is a condition characterized by an abnormally high level of potassium in the blood.
    • Potassium is crucial for normal cell function, especially in the heart, muscles, and nerves.
    • Causes include kidney dysfunction, excessive potassium intake, and certain medications.
    • Symptoms can include muscle fatigue, weakness, paralysis, and abnormal heart rhythms.
  • Hypokalemia
    • Hypokalemia is a condition where there is a lower than normal level of potassium in the blood.
    • It can result from conditions like chronic kidney disease, excessive loss of potassium through urine, or inadequate potassium intake.
    • Symptoms may include muscle cramps, weakness, fatigue, and cardiac arrhythmias.
    • Treatment typically involves potassium supplements and addressing the underlying cause.
  • Hypernatremia
    • Hypernatremia is a condition where the sodium level in the blood is higher than normal.
    • It often occurs due to dehydration, water loss, or excessive sodium intake.
    • Symptoms can include thirst, confusion, muscle twitching, and, in severe cases, seizures or coma.
    • Treatment focuses on slowly rehydrating the patient and addressing the cause of the sodium imbalance.

  • They are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution, covering Articles 36 to 51.
  • The DPSPs aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life and also establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.

Additional Information

  • Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)
    • The DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.However, they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to establish a just society.

    • Despite being non-justiciable, they are fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to establish social and economic democracy.
  • Relation with Fundamental Rights
    • Fundamental Rights and DPSPs together form the conscience of the Indian Constitution.
    • While Fundamental Rights are justiciable and enforceable by the courts, DPSPs are non-justiciable.
    • Both aim to establish social, economic, and political justice in the country.
    • In case of conflict, the courts have generally given precedence to Fundamental Rights over DPSPs.
  • Amendments and DPSP

questions.question: A boatman rows to a place 30 km distant and back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 10 km with the stream at the same time as 4 km against the stream. Find the speed (in km/h) of the stream.
questions.questionHtml: A boatman rows to a place 30 km distant and back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 10 km with the stream at the same time as 4 km against the stream. Find the speed (in km/h) of the stream.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Downstream speed (D) : Upstream speed (U) = Distance Ratio (in same time) = 10 : 4 = 5 : 2.

Let D = 5k and U = 2k. Total time = (30 ÷ 5k) + (30 ÷ 2k) = 14 ⇒ 6/k + 15/k = 14 ⇒ 21/k = 14 ⇒ k = 3/2.

Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2 = (5k − 2k) ÷ 2 = 3k/2.

Substitute k = 3/2 ⇒ Speed of stream = (3 × 3/2) ÷ 2 = 9/4 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 9/4 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total distance for a one-way trip = 30 km.

Total time for the round trip = 14 hours.

Distance covered downstream in a given time = 10 km.

Distance covered upstream in the same time = 4 km.

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed of stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

Calculations:

Let the speed of the boat in still water be u km/h and the speed of the stream be v km/h.

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = u + v

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = u − v

Since the time taken is the same for 10 km downstream and 4 km upstream:

⇒ 10 ÷ (u + v) = 4 ÷ (u − v)

⇒ (u + v) ÷ (u − v) = 10/4 = 5/2

Let Downstream speed D = 5k and Upstream speed U = 2k.

Total time taken for the round trip is 14 hours:

⇒ 30 ÷ D + 30 ÷ U = 14

⇒ 30 ÷ 5k + 30 ÷ 2k = 14

⇒ 6/k + 15/k = 14

⇒ 21/k = 14

⇒ k = 21 ÷ 14 = 3/2

Now, calculate the absolute speeds D and U:

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = 5 × 3/2 = 15/2 = 7.5 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = 2 × 3/2 = 3 km/h

Speed of the stream (v) = (D − U) ÷ 2

⇒ v = (7.5 − 3) ÷ 2 = 4.5 ÷ 2 = 9/4 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 9/4 km/h.

Additional Information

Downstream and Upstream Speeds

When a boat moves with the stream, its effective speed increases (D = u + v). When it moves against the stream, its effective speed decreases (U = u − v).

Boat in Still Water

The speed of a boat in still water (u) can be calculated directly if downstream and upstream speeds are known: u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

The speed of the stream or current (v) is half the difference between the downstream and upstream speeds: v = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Constant Time Principle

If the time taken to travel two different distances is the same, the ratio of the distances is directly proportional to the ratio of their respective speeds (D1 ÷ D2 = S1 ÷ S2).

questions.question: Two circles, centred at P and Q intersect at two points C and D. AB is tangent to the two circles at A and B. If ∠ADB = 68°, then ∠ACB = ________.
questions.questionHtml: Two circles, centred at P and Q intersect at two points C and D. AB is tangent to the two circles at A and B. If ∠ADB = 68°, then ∠ACB = ________.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two intersecting circles with a common tangent AB, and intersection points C and D:

The sum of the angles subtended by the common tangent at the intersection points is always 180°.

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ADB = 180°

⇒ ∠ACB + 68° = 180°

⇒ ∠ACB = 112°

∴ The correct answer is 112°.

Alternate Method

Given:

∠ADB = 68°

Formula Used:

Alternate Segment Theorem: The angle between a tangent and a chord is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

Sum of interior angles of a triangle is 180°.

Calculations:

⇒ Let AB be the common tangent touching the circles at A and B.

⇒ By the Alternate Segment Theorem for the first circle, the angle between tangent AB and chord AC is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠BAC = ∠ADC

⇒ Similarly, for the second circle, the angle between tangent AB and chord BC is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠ABC = ∠BDC

⇒ In ΔABC, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠BAC + ∠ABC = 180°

⇒ Substituting the corresponding alternate angles into the equation:

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ADC + ∠BDC = 180°

⇒ We know from the figure that ∠ADC + ∠BDC = ∠ADB.

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ADB = 180°

⇒ ∠ACB + 68° = 180°

⇒ ∠ACB = 180° − 68°

⇒ ∠ACB = 112°

∴ The correct answer is 112°.

Additional Information

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact is strictly equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

Length of DCT = √(d2 − (r1 − r2)2), where d is the distance between the centres and r1, r2 are the radii.

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

Length of TCT = √(d2 − (r1 + r2)2), applicable when circles are strictly disjoint.

Common Chord of Intersecting Circles

The line joining the centres of two intersecting circles acts as the perpendicular bisector of their common chord.

questions.question: Find the remainder: \((17^{13} - 21) \div 18\)
questions.questionHtml: Find the remainder: \((17^{13} - 21) \div 18\)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

17 ÷ 18 gives a remainder of −1, so 1713 ÷ 18 gives a remainder of (−1)13 = −1.

21 ÷ 18 gives a remainder of 3.

Combined remainder = −1 − 3 = −4.

Since the remainder is negative, add the divisor: 18 − 4 = 14.

∴ The correct answer is 14.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: (1713 − 21) ÷ 18

Concept Used:

Remainder Theorem: When dividing a polynomial by (x − a), the remainder is found by evaluating the expression at x = a.

Calculations:

⇒ We can express the base 17 as (18 − 1).

⇒ The given expression becomes: ((18 − 1)13 − 21) ÷ 18

⇒ When expanding (18 − 1)13 using the binomial theorem, all terms containing 18 are perfectly divisible by 18.

⇒ The only remaining term from the expansion is the constant term: (−1)13 = −1.

⇒ Now, divide the constant 21 by 18, which gives a remainder of 3.

⇒ Total remainder expression = −1 − 3 = −4.

⇒ A remainder of −4 means the value is 4 less than the divisor.

⇒ Actual positive remainder = 18 − 4 = 14.

∴ The correct answer is 14.

Additional Information

Remainder of an ÷ (a+1)

When an is divided by (a+1), the remainder is 1 if n is an even number, and the remainder is 'a' (or −1) if n is an odd number.

Remainder of an ÷ (a−1)

When an is divided by (a−1), the remainder is always 1, regardless of whether the power n is odd or even.

Negative Remainder Concept

A negative remainder mathematically indicates how much less the number is from the next multiple of the divisor. The actual positive remainder is obtained by adding the divisor: Actual Remainder = Divisor − Negative Remainder.

questions.question: Simplify the following. 16 ÷ 2− 7 × 15 ÷ 3 + 5 × 5 + 4 × 3 − 10

16 ÷ 2− 7 × 15 ÷ 3 + 5 × 5 + 4 × 3 − 10
questions.solution:

Formula Used:

Apply the BODMAS/BIDMAS rule (Brackets, Orders (i.e. powers and square roots, etc.), Division and Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction)

Calculation:

Start with division and multiplication from left to right:

16 ÷ 2 = 8

7 × 15 = 105

105 ÷ 3 = 35

5 × 5 = 25

4 × 3 = 12

Now substitute these values back into the expression:

8 - 35 + 25 + 12 - 10

Next, perform addition and subtraction from left to right:

8 - 35 = -27

-27 + 25 = -2

-2 + 12 = 10

10 - 10 = 0

The simplified result is 0.

The correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: If the curved surface area of a cylinder is 880 cm 2 , then the product of its height and radius is:
questions.questionHtml: If the curved surface area of a cylinder is 880 cm<sup>2</sup>, then the product of its height and radius is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of cylinder = 2πrh

Given 2πrh = 880

r × h = 880 ÷ (2 × 22 ÷ 7)

r × h = 880 × (7 ÷ 44) = 140

∴ The correct answer is 140 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Curved surface area of the cylinder = 880 cm2

Formula Used:

Curved surface area of a cylinder = 2πrh

Where r = radius and h = height

Calculations:

⇒ 2 × (22 ÷ 7) × r × h = 880

⇒ (44 ÷ 7) × r × h = 880

⇒ r × h = 880 × (7 ÷ 44)

⇒ r × h = 20 × 7

⇒ r × h = 140 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 140 cm2.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Volume of Cylinder

The volume represents the total space occupied by the cylinder: V = πr2h.

Surface Area of Cone

For a cone with base radius r and slant height l, the Curved Surface Area = πrl and Total Surface Area = πr(r + l).

questions.question: The angle turned by minutes hand in 25 minutes in a clock is:
questions.questionHtml: The angle turned by minutes hand in 25 minutes in a clock is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The minute hand covers 2π radians (a full circle) in 60 minutes.

Angle turned in 1 minute = 2π ÷ 60 = π/30 radians.

Angle turned in 25 minutes = 25 × π/30 = 5π/6 radians.

∴ The correct answer is 5π/6 radians.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time duration for which the minute hand turned = 25 minutes

Formula Used:

Angle (in radians) = (Given minutes ÷ Total minutes in 1 hour) × 2π

Calculations:

⇒ Total minutes in a complete clock revolution = 60 minutes

⇒ Fraction of the clock covered by the minute hand = 25 ÷ 60 = 5/12

⇒ The total angle for one full revolution = 360° = 2π radians

⇒ Angle turned in 25 minutes = (5/12) × 2π

⇒ Angle turned = 10π ÷ 12 = 5π/6 radians

∴ The correct answer is 5π/6 radians.

Additional Information

Speed of the Minute Hand

The minute hand moves at a constant speed of 6° per minute (which is equivalent to π/30 radians per minute).

Speed of the Hour Hand

The hour hand moves much slower at a speed of 0.5° per minute (which is equivalent to π/360 radians per minute).

Angle Between Clock Hands

The exact internal angle θ between the hour and minute hand at H hours and M minutes can be calculated using the formula: θ = |30H − 11/2 M| degrees.

Degrees to Radians Conversion

To convert an angle from degrees into radians, simply multiply the value by π/180. For example, an angle of 150° corresponds to 150° × (π/180) = 5π/6 radians.

questions.question: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 72. What is the average score of the class?
questions.questionHtml: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 72. What is the average score of the class?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of number of students in the two groups = 12 : 18 ⇒ 2 : 3.

Let the assumed average of the class be 62 (the average of the first group).

Deviation of the second group from the assumed average = 72 − 62 = +10.

Net average deviation = (3 × 10) ÷ (2 + 3) = 30 ÷ 5 = +6.

Overall average = Assumed Average + Net deviation = 62 + 6 = 68.

∴ The correct answer is 68.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total number of students = 30

Average score of 12 students = 62

Average score of the remaining students = 72

Formula Used:

Overall Average = (Total sum of all scores) ÷ (Total number of students)

Calculations:

⇒ Number of remaining students = 30 − 12 = 18

⇒ Sum of scores of 12 students = 12 × 62 = 744

⇒ Sum of scores of 18 students = 18 × 72 = 1296

⇒ Total sum of scores of 30 students = 744 + 1296 = 2040

⇒ Overall Average = 2040 ÷ 30 = 68

∴ The correct answer is 68.

Additional Information

Weighted Average

When two groups with sizes N1 and N2 have averages A1 and A2 respectively, the combined average is calculated as (N1A1 + N2A2) ÷ (N1 + N2).

Deviation Method

To simplify calculations, select an assumed average. The overall average equals the assumed average plus the net deviation divided by the total number of observations.

Alligation Method

The ratio in which two quantities are mixed is inversely proportional to the differences of their individual averages from the overall average.

questions.question: If m = a secA and y = b tanA, then find the value of b 2 m 2 - a 2 y 2 + \(\frac{a^2 y^2}{b^2 m^2}\) + cos 2 A.
questions.questionHtml: If m = a secA and y = b tanA, then find the value of b2m2 - a2y2 + \(\frac{a^2 y^2}{b^2 m^2}\) + cos2A.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put A = 45° ⇒ m = a sec 45° = a√2 and y = b tan 45° = b

Substitute in b2m2 − a2y2 + (a2y2) / (b2m2) + cos2A

⇒ b2(a√2)2 − a2(b)2 + (a2b2) / (b2(a√2)2) + cos245°

⇒ 2a2b2 − a2b2 + (a2b2) / (2a2b2) + (1/√2)2

⇒ a2b2 + 1/2 + 1/2 = a2b2 + 1

∴ The correct answer is a2b2 + 1.

Alternate Method

Given:

m = a secA ⇒ secA = m/a

y = b tanA ⇒ tanA = y/b

Formula Used:

sec2A − tan2A = 1

sin2A + cos2A = 1

Calculations:

⇒ (m/a)2 − (y/b)2 = 1

⇒ (b2m2 − a2y2) / (a2b2) = 1

⇒ b2m2 − a2y2 = a2b2

Evaluating the fractional term:

⇒ (a2y2) / (b2m2) = (a2b2 tan2A) / (a2b2 sec2A)

⇒ tan2A / sec2A = (sin2A / cos2A) × cos2A = sin2A

Substitute these calculated values into the main expression:

⇒ b2m2 − a2y2 + (a2y2) / (b2m2) + cos2A

⇒ a2b2 + sin2A + cos2A

⇒ a2b2 + 1

∴ The correct answer is a2b2 + 1.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

sec2θ − tan2θ = 1

cosec2θ − cot2θ = 1

Trigonometric Conversions

tanθ = sinθ / cosθ ⇒ tanθ × cosθ = sinθ

secθ = 1 / cosθ ⇒ secθ × cosθ = 1

questions.question: Two pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 36 minutes and 45 minutes, respectively. If both pipes are opened together, the time taken to fill the tank is:
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 36 minutes and 45 minutes, respectively. If both pipes are opened together, the time taken to fill the tank is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two pipes can fill a tank in x and y minutes individually, the time taken to fill the tank together is (x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Time taken = (36 × 45) ÷ (36 + 45)

⇒ Time taken = 1620 ÷ 81

⇒ Time taken = 20 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 20 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Pipe P to fill the tank = 36 minutes

Time taken by Pipe Q to fill the tank = 45 minutes

Calculations:

Total capacity of the tank = LCM of 36 and 45 = 180 units

Pipe Time (minutes) Total Work Efficiency
P 36 180 180 ÷ 36 = 5
Q 45 180 ÷ 45 = 4

⇒ Combined efficiency of P and Q = 5 + 4 = 9 units/minute

⇒ Time taken to fill the tank together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 180 ÷ 9

⇒ Time taken = 20 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 20 minutes.

Additional Information

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank and its work (efficiency) is always taken as positive. An outlet pipe empties the tank and its work (efficiency) is always taken as negative.

Unitary Method for Time & Work

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, the part of the tank filled in 1 hour is 1/x. If two pipes operate simultaneously, their 1 hour work is given by (1/x + 1/y).

Three Pipes Working Together

If three pipes A, B and C have efficiencies ea, eb, and ec respectively, the total time required to fill a tank is calculated as Total Capacity ÷ (ea + eb + ec).

questions.question: A manufacturer announces a trade discount of 30% on his products for his dealers. One of the dealers purchased 6 smartphones manufactured by the company at the rate of Rs.25,000 each. What is the amount of trade discount?
questions.questionHtml: A manufacturer announces a trade discount of 30% on his products for his dealers. One of the dealers purchased 6 smartphones manufactured by the company at the rate of Rs.25,000 each. What is the amount of trade discount?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total list price of 6 smartphones = 6 × 25000 = Rs. 1,50,000

Trade discount = 30% of Total list price

Trade discount = (30 ÷ 100) × 1,50,000 = Rs. 45,000

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 45,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number of smartphones purchased = 6

Price of each smartphone = Rs. 25,000

Trade discount percentage = 30%

Formula Used:

Total List Price = Number of items × Price per item

Discount Amount = Total List Price × (Discount % ÷ 100)

Calculations:

⇒ Total List Price = 6 × 25,000

⇒ Total List Price = Rs. 1,50,000

⇒ Discount Amount = 1,50,000 × (30 ÷ 100)

⇒ Discount Amount = 1,50,000 × 0.30

⇒ Discount Amount = Rs. 45,000

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 45,000.

Additional Information

Trade Discount

It is a reduction in the list price of goods allowed by a manufacturer or wholesaler to retailers, typically for bulk purchases. It is not recorded individually in accounting books.

Cash Discount

A cash discount is allowed to encourage prompt payment. It is always calculated on the net invoice price (i.e., List Price − Trade Discount).

Successive Discounts

When two discounts a% and b% are given successively, the effective discount percentage is given by the formula: Effective Discount = (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: Find the mean proportional of 12.96 and 0.16.
questions.questionHtml: Find the mean proportional of 12.96 and 0.16.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Required Mean = √(12.96 × 0.16)

We know that √12.96 = 3.6 and √0.16 = 0.4

⇒ Mean = 3.6 × 0.4 = 1.44

∴ The correct answer is 1.44.

Alternate Method

Given:

First number (a) = 12.96

Second number (b) = 0.16

Formula Used:

Mean proportional (x) = √(a × b)

Calculations:

⇒ x = √(12.96 × 0.16)

⇒ x = √( (1296 ÷ 100) × (16 ÷ 100) )

⇒ x = √(20736 ÷ 10000)

⇒ x = 144 ÷ 100

⇒ x = 1.44

∴ The correct answer is 1.44.

Additional Information

Third Proportional

If a : b :: b : c, then c is called the third proportional to a and b. Formula: c = b2 ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If a : b :: c : d, then d is called the fourth proportional to a, b, and c. Formula: d = (b × c) ÷ a.

First Proportional

If a : b :: c : d, then a is called the first proportional to b, c, and d. Formula: a = (b × c) ÷ d.

questions.question: The perimeters of two similar triangles ΔRST and ΔABC are 26 cm and 39 cm, respectively. If AB = 24 cm, then RS is __.
questions.questionHtml: The perimeters of two similar triangles ΔRST and ΔABC are 26 cm and 39 cm, respectively. If AB = 24 cm, then RS is __.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding sides is equal to the ratio of their perimeters.

⇒ RS ÷ AB = Perimeter of ΔRST ÷ Perimeter of ΔABC

⇒ RS ÷ 24 = 26 ÷ 39

⇒ RS ÷ 24 = 2 ÷ 3

⇒ RS = 16 cm

∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Perimeter of ΔRST = 26 cm

Perimeter of ΔABC = 39 cm

Side AB = 24 cm

Formula Used:

For two similar triangles, the ratio of their perimeters is strictly equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

⇒ If ΔRST ∼ ΔABC, then Perimeter(ΔRST) ÷ Perimeter(ΔABC) = RS ÷ AB

Calculations:

⇒ 26 ÷ 39 = RS ÷ 24

⇒ 2 ÷ 3 = RS ÷ 24

⇒ RS = (2 × 24) ÷ 3

⇒ RS = 48 ÷ 3

⇒ RS = 16 cm

∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.

Additional Information

Ratio of Areas of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides. Area(Δ1) ÷ Area(Δ2) = (Side1 ÷ Side2)2.

Ratio of Perimeters of Similar Triangles

The ratio of perimeters is exactly equal to the ratio of corresponding sides, altitudes, or medians. P1 ÷ P2 = S1 ÷ S2.

Congruence vs Similarity

Congruent triangles are identical in both shape and size (ratio 1:1), whereas similar triangles have the same shape but are proportionally scaled relative to each other.

questions.question: In the following sets, which set represents the angles of a triangle?
questions.questionHtml: In the following sets, which set represents the angles of a triangle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

According to the angle sum property of triangles, the sum of all three interior angles must equal exactly 180°.

We can quickly sum the values in each option to find the valid set.

Sum of {30°, 60°, 90°} = 30° + 60° + 90° = 180°, which perfectly forms a valid triangle.

∴ The correct answer is {30°, 60°, 90°}.

Alternate Method

Given:

Four sets of possible angles for a triangle:

1. {30°, 60°, 90°}

2. {80°, 50°, 90°}

3. {30°, 50°, 110°}

4. {30°, 50°, 90°}

Formula Used:

The sum of the interior angles of a valid triangle is exactly 180°.

Calculations:

We check the sum of the angles for each given option:

⇒ Option 1: 30° + 60° + 90° = 180° (Valid Triangle)

⇒ Option 2: 80° + 50° + 90° = 220° (Invalid)

⇒ Option 3: 30° + 50° + 110° = 190° (Invalid)

⇒ Option 4: 30° + 50° + 90° = 170° (Invalid)

⇒ Only the first set of angles gives a sum of exactly 180°.

∴ The correct answer is {30°, 60°, 90°}.

Additional Information

Types of Triangles by Angles

Acute Triangle (all angles < 90°), Right Triangle (one angle = 90°), and Obtuse Triangle (one angle > 90°).

Exterior Angle Property

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any valid triangle, the sum of the lengths of any two sides must always be strictly greater than the length of the remaining third side.

questions.question: Simplify the following expression. ( g − h ) 2 − ( g + h ) 2 + 4 g h
questions.questionHtml:
Simplify the following expression.
(g−h)2−(g+h)2+4gh
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

We know the standard algebraic identity: (a + b)2 − (a − b)2 = 4ab.

By reversing the terms, we get: (a − b)2 − (a + b)2 = −4ab.

Substitute a = g and b = h directly into the given expression.

⇒ (g − h)2 − (g + h)2 + 4gh = −4gh + 4gh = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: (g − h)2 − (g + h)2 + 4gh

Formula Used:

(a − b)2 = a2 + b2 − 2ab

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

Calculations:

Expand the first term (g − h)2:

⇒ g2 + h2 − 2gh

Expand the second term (g + h)2:

⇒ g2 + h2 + 2gh

Substitute both expansions back into the original expression:

⇒ (g2 + h2 − 2gh) − (g2 + h2 + 2gh) + 4gh

Distribute the negative sign over the second term:

⇒ g2 + h2 − 2gh − g2 − h2 − 2gh + 4gh

Group the like terms together:

⇒ (g2 − g2) + (h2 − h2) − 2gh − 2gh + 4gh

⇒ 0 + 0 − 4gh + 4gh

⇒ 0

∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information

Sum of Squares Identity

When adding the squares of sum and difference, the middle terms cancel out: (a + b)2 + (a − b)2 = 2(a2 + b2).

Difference of Squares

The difference between the squares of two terms can be factored into a product: a2 − b2 = (a − b)(a + b).

Cube Formulas

The sum and difference formulas for perfect cubes are frequently used in simplification: (a ± b)3 = a3 ± b3 ± 3ab(a ± b).

questions.question: A sum of ₹10,000 is taken as a loan by Rajesh at a rate of 15% p.a. simple interest for 2 years. But Rajesh could not repay it at the agreed time and asked for an extension of two more years. So, the lender included the interest amount for the period as principal for the next two years at the same rate of interest. The total amount paid by Rajesh at the end of 4 years is: Ans
questions.questionHtml:
A sum of ₹10,000 is taken as a loan by Rajesh at a rate of 15% p.a. simple interest for 2 years. But Rajesh could not repay it at the agreed time and asked for an extension of two more years. So, the lender included the interest amount for the period as principal for the next two years at the same rate of interest. The total amount paid by Rajesh at the end of 4 years is:
Ans
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Simple Interest (SI) percentage for 2 years at 15% p.a. = 15 × 2 = 30%.

Amount after the first 2 years = 10000 × 1.30 = ₹13,000.

The lender includes the interest in the principal, so the new principal for the next 2 years is ₹13,000.

Amount after the next 2 years = 13000 × 1.30 = ₹16,900.

∴ The correct answer is ₹16,900.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Principal (P1) = ₹10,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 15% p.a.

Time period (T1) = 2 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

Calculations:

⇒ SI for the first 2 years = (10000 × 15 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹3,000

⇒ Amount at the end of 2 years = 10000 + 3000 = ₹13,000

⇒ The new principal for the next 2 years (P2) = ₹13,000

⇒ SI for the next 2 years = (13000 × 15 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹3,900

⇒ Total amount paid = P2 + SI for the next 2 years = 13000 + 3900 = ₹16,900

∴ The correct answer is ₹16,900.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

Simple interest is calculated uniformly on the initial principal throughout the loan period. The generic formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

The total amount paid at the end of the term is the sum of the principal and the interest earned. Amount = P + SI.

Compounding Effect in SI

If simple interest is added to the principal midway during an extended period, the subsequent interest is calculated on the new increased principal. This effectively functions like compound interest for the new term block.

questions.question: The area of a sector of a circle of radius 12 cm, formed by an arc of length 7 cm is:
questions.questionHtml: The area of a sector of a circle of radius 12 cm, formed by an arc of length 7 cm is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the arc length and radius of a sector are given, its area can be found directly using the formula:

Area = ½ × l × r

Where l = length of the arc, and r = radius of the circle.

⇒ Area = ½ × 7 × 12

⇒ Area = 7 × 6 = 42 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 42 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the sector (r) = 12 cm

Length of the arc (l) = 7 cm

Formula Used:

Angle subtended at the centre, θ = Arc length ÷ Radius (in radians)

Area of a sector = ½ × r2 × θ

Calculations:

⇒ θ = l ÷ r = 7 ÷ 12 radians

⇒ Area of the sector = ½ × (12)2 × (7 ÷ 12)

⇒ Area = ½ × 144 × (7 ÷ 12)

⇒ Area = ½ × 12 × 7

⇒ Area = 6 × 7 = 42 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 42 cm2.

Additional Information

Area of Sector (Degree Measure)

If the central angle is given in degrees (θ), the area of the sector is calculated as Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr2.

Length of an Arc (Degree Measure)

The length of an arc that subtends an angle θ at the centre is given by l = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Perimeter of a Sector

The total perimeter of a sector consists of the arc length along with the two enclosing radii. Thus, Perimeter = l + 2r.

questions.question: Kalyan spends 80% of his income. His income increases by 15% and his expenditure also increases by 5%. The percentage of increase in his savings is:
questions.questionHtml: Kalyan spends 80% of his income. His income increases by 15% and his expenditure also increases by 5%. The percentage of increase in his savings is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Expenditure to Savings = 80% : 20% = 4 : 1.

We apply the weighted average method: Income = Expenditure + Savings.

Change in Income = (Exp Ratio × Exp Change + Sav Ratio × Sav Change) ÷ Total Ratio

⇒ 15% = (4 × 5% + 1 × x%) ÷ 5

⇒ 75% = 20% + x% ⇒ x = 55%

∴ The correct answer is 55%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Kalyan spends 80% of his income.

Increase in income = 15%.

Increase in expenditure = 5%.

Formula Used:

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase Value ÷ Initial Value) × 100

Calculation:

⇒ Let initial income be 100 units.

⇒ Initial expenditure = 80% of 100 = 80 units

⇒ Initial savings = 100 − 80 = 20 units

⇒ After a 15% increase, new income = 100 + 15 = 115 units

⇒ After a 5% increase, new expenditure = 80 + (5% of 80) = 80 + 4 = 84 units

⇒ New savings = New income − New expenditure = 115 − 84 = 31 units

⇒ Increase in savings = 31 − 20 = 11 units

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (11 ÷ 20) × 100 = 55%

∴ The correct answer is 55%.

Additional Information

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The basic relationship is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any percentage change in income impacts both expenditure and savings proportional to their initial distributions.

Percentage Change Formula

The percentage change is always calculated on the base original value: % Change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Weighted Average (Alligation) Method

When a whole is divided into two parts in the ratio n1 : n2, the net percentage change can be calculated directly as: Net % = (n1 × x1 + n2 × x2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

questions.question: A dishonest fruit-seller sells fruits at 20% profit but he uses 950 gm weight in place of 1 kg. What is the profit per cent?
questions.questionHtml: A dishonest fruit-seller sells fruits at 20% profit but he uses 950 gm weight in place of 1 kg. What is the profit per cent?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio 1 (Profit on Price): 100 → 120 = 5 : 6

Ratio 2 (Profit on Weight): 950 → 1000 = 19 : 20

Net Ratio (CP : SP) = (5 × 19) : (6 × 20) = 95 : 120 = 19 : 24

Profit % = [(24 − 19) / 19] × 100 = 5/19 × 100 = 500/19 %

∴ The correct option is (B).

Alternate Method

Given:

Declared Profit % = 20%

False Weight = 950 gm instead of 1 kg (1000 gm)

Formula Used:

Overall Profit % = [(Total SP − Effective CP) / Effective CP] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of 1 gm = Re. 1

⇒ CP of 1000 gm = Rs. 1000

⇒ Seller sells 1 kg at 20% profit, so SP = 1000 + 20% of 1000 = Rs. 1200

⇒ Seller uses 950 gm instead of 1000 gm, so Effective CP = Rs. 950

⇒ Total Profit = SP − Effective CP = 1200 − 950 = Rs. 250

⇒ Profit % = (Profit / Effective CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (250 / 950) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 25/95 × 100 = 5/19 × 100 = 500/19 %

∴ The correct option is (B).

Additional Information

Dishonest Dealer Weight Profit

Profit % due to false weight = [ (True Weight − False Weight) / False Weight ] × 100

Combined Profit Rule

If a dealer sells at x% profit and uses y% less weight, the overall profit multiplier is [(100 + x) / (100 − y)].

Successive Percentage for Profit

Total Gain % = [ (100 + g1)/100 × (100 + g2)/100 − 1 ] × 100, where g1 and g2 are individual gains.

questions.question: Simplify \(\frac{1.5 \times 1.5 + 2.5 \times 2.5 + 3.5 \times 3.5 + 2 \times 1.5 \times 2.5 + 2 \times 2.5 \times 3.5 + 2 \times 1.5 \times 3.5}{1.5 + 2.5 + 3.5}\) .
questions.questionHtml: Simplify \(\frac{1.5 \times 1.5 + 2.5 \times 2.5 + 3.5 \times 3.5 + 2 \times 1.5 \times 2.5 + 2 \times 2.5 \times 3.5 + 2 \times 1.5 \times 3.5}{1.5 + 2.5 + 3.5}\).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The expression follows the algebraic pattern: (a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca) ÷ (a + b + c).

By using the standard identity, the numerator is equivalent to (a + b + c)2.

Thus, the given expression simplifies directly to (a + b + c).

Here, substituting a = 1.5, b = 2.5, and c = 3.5.

Result = 1.5 + 2.5 + 3.5 = 7.5.

∴ The correct answer is 7.5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: (1.5 × 1.5 + 2.5 × 2.5 + 3.5 × 3.5 + 2 × 1.5 × 2.5 + 2 × 2.5 × 3.5 + 2 × 1.5 × 3.5) ÷ (1.5 + 2.5 + 3.5)

Formula Used:

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca

Calculation:

Let a = 1.5, b = 2.5, and c = 3.5

⇒ Numerator = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca

⇒ Numerator = (a + b + c)2

⇒ Denominator = a + b + c

⇒ Expression = (a + b + c)2 ÷ (a + b + c)

⇒ Expression = a + b + c

⇒ Expression = 1.5 + 2.5 + 3.5

⇒ Expression = 7.5

∴ The correct answer is 7.5.

Additional Information

Square of a Binomial

(a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2 and (a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2

Difference of Squares

a2 − b2 = (a − b)(a + b)

Sum of Cubes Identity

a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ca)

Conditional Zero Sum

If a + b + c = 0, then a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc

questions.question: The value of \(\left(\frac{cosecA}{cosecA-1} + \frac{cosecA}{cosecA+1}\right)\left(\frac{secA}{secA-1} + \frac{secA}{secA+1}\right)^{-1}\) , when A = 60° is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\left(\frac{cosecA}{cosecA-1} + \frac{cosecA}{cosecA+1}\right)\left(\frac{secA}{secA-1} + \frac{secA}{secA+1}\right)^{-1}\), when A = 60° is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Substitute A = 60° directly (cosec 60° = 2/√3, sec 60° = 2).

First term = (2/√3) ÷ (2/√3 − 1) + (2/√3) ÷ (2/√3 + 1) = 2/(2 − √3) + 2/(2 + √3).

First term = 2(2 + √3) + 2(2 − √3) = 8.

Second term = 2 ÷ (2 − 1) + 2 ÷ (2 + 1) = 2/1 + 2/3 = 8/3.

Given expression = 8 × (8/3)−1 = 8 × 3/8 = 3.

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: [cosecA / (cosecA − 1) + cosecA / (cosecA + 1)] × [secA / (secA − 1) + secA / (secA + 1)]−1

Calculations:

⇒ Let's simplify the first part:

⇒ cosecA / (cosecA − 1) + cosecA / (cosecA + 1)

⇒ = cosecA × [ (cosecA + 1 + cosecA − 1) ÷ (cosec2A − 1) ]

⇒ = cosecA × [ 2cosecA ÷ cot2A ] = 2cosec2A ÷ cot2A

⇒ = 2(1/sin2A) ÷ (cos2A/sin2A) = 2/cos2A = 2sec2A

⇒ Now, simplify the second part:

⇒ secA / (secA − 1) + secA / (secA + 1)

⇒ = secA × [ (secA + 1 + secA − 1) ÷ (sec2A − 1) ]

⇒ = secA × [ 2secA ÷ tan2A ] = 2sec2A ÷ tan2A

⇒ = 2(1/cos2A) ÷ (sin2A/cos2A) = 2/sin2A = 2cosec2A

⇒ Substitute both simplified parts into the original expression:

⇒ Result = 2sec2A × (2cosec2A)−1 = 2sec2A ÷ 2cosec2A

⇒ Result = (1/cos2A) ÷ (1/sin2A) = sin2A ÷ cos2A = tan2A

⇒ Given A = 60°, substitute the value:

⇒ tan260° = (√3)2 = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Important squared identities: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 | sec2θ − tan2θ = 1 | cosec2θ − cot2θ = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

sinθ = 1 ÷ cosecθ | cosθ = 1 ÷ secθ | tanθ = 1 ÷ cotθ.

Standard Values at 60°

sin 60° = √3/2 | cos 60° = 1/2 | tan 60° = √3 | sec 60° = 2 | cosec 60° = 2/√3.

questions.question: 2 biscuits and 1 chocolate cost ₹69. 2 chocolates and 3 cups of coffee cost ₹127. 3 biscuits, 4 chocolates and 2 cups of coffee cost ₹229. Find the total cost (in ₹) of 5 biscuits, 5 chocolates and 5 cups of coffee.
questions.questionHtml: 2 biscuits and 1 chocolate cost ₹69. 2 chocolates and 3 cups of coffee cost ₹127. 3 biscuits, 4 chocolates and 2 cups of coffee cost ₹229. Find the total cost (in ₹) of 5 biscuits, 5 chocolates and 5 cups of coffee.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let b, c, and f be the unit prices of biscuit, chocolate, and coffee.

Given: 2b + c = 69; 2c + 3f = 127; 3b + 4c + 2f = 229.

From the first, c = 69 − 2b. Substitute this in the other two equations:

4b − 3f = 11 and 5b − 2f = 47. Solving these gives b = 17, f = 19.

Hence, c = 69 − 2(17) = 35. Total cost of 1 set = 17 + 35 + 19 = 71.

∴ The correct answer is ₹355.

Alternate Method

Let the cost of 1 biscuit, 1 chocolate, and 1 coffee be b, c, and f respectively.

Given:

⇒ 2b + c = 69   --- (1)

⇒ 2c + 3f = 127   --- (2)

⇒ 3b + 4c + 2f = 229   --- (3)

From (1), we get c = 69 − 2b.

Substitute c in (2):

⇒ 2(69 − 2b) + 3f = 127

⇒ 138 − 4b + 3f = 127

⇒ 4b − 3f = 11   --- (4)

Substitute c in (3):

⇒ 3b + 4(69 − 2b) + 2f = 229

⇒ 3b + 276 − 8b + 2f = 229

⇒ 5b − 2f = 47   --- (5)

Multiply (4) by 2 and (5) by 3:

⇒ 8b − 6f = 22

⇒ 15b − 6f = 141

Subtracting the first equation from the second:

⇒ 7b = 119 ⇒ b = 17

Putting b = 17 in (1):

⇒ 2(17) + c = 69 ⇒ c = 69 − 34 = 35

Putting c = 35 in (2):

⇒ 2(35) + 3f = 127 ⇒ 3f = 127 − 70 = 57 ⇒ f = 19

Total cost of 5 of each item = 5 × (b + c + f)

⇒ 5 × (17 + 35 + 19) = 5 × 71 = 355

∴ The correct answer is ₹355.

Additional Information

System of Linear Equations

A collection of one or more linear equations involving the same variables. They can be solved systematically using substitution, elimination, or matrix methods to find the unique solution values.

Substitution Method

A method for solving systems of equations by expressing one variable in terms of the others and substituting it into the remaining equations to reduce the number of variables.

Elimination Method

A process of multiplying equations by specific constants so that adding or subtracting them eliminates one of the variables entirely, allowing for easier resolution.
